author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: October's flat CPI, a 0.5% producer-price drop and softer retail sales have flipped markets from 'higher for longer' to 'the Fed is done', producing a 20-observation bull flattening, a weaker dollar and a broadening rally into small caps, banks, REITs and Hong Kong platforms, funded by a sharp energy sell-off. The long end has not fully bought it (10Y up 4 bps over five observations after a weak 30-year auction and Moody's negative outlook), so we favour rate-sensitive cyclicals and belly duration over the 30Y, with the growth-scare risk (Japan's GDP contraction, Europe's fiscal shock, a possible U.S. recession-rule trigger) as the main threat; Poland is the standout regional long on political change, with NBP conflict and revised-up CPI as the divergence.
sources_policy: Only the 2023-11-16 frozen feed (tools/digest.py) and the 2023-11-16 market card (tools/showcard.py) were used. Every concrete fact is tied to a cited headline in the same paragraph or to a card field; numbers come from the card or a same-paragraph cited headline title. No numeric spot-FX; currency direction comes only from cited headlines. No other date's feed, card, spec or draft was opened, and no web resource was used. Pending events (Walmart's print, a Tusk government, China's housing package, a spot-bitcoin ETF decision) are described as pending without dates because no cited preview dates them.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n1505 (Reuters, US Senate passes stopgap funding bill; stamped 2023-11-15 08:00, date-only): the Senate vote most likely took place on the evening of 2023-11-15 U.S. Eastern time, i.e. after 2023-11-16 00:00 UTC, so Senate passage is not stated; only House passage (n1504) and the bill going to the Senate (n1478) are used.

n0131 (NPR, Biden announces fentanyl/military-talk agreements), n0132 (Al Jazeera, 'real progress' after four hours of talks), n0142 (Reuters TAKEAWAYS), n0138 (Atlantic Council experts react) and n0144 (PBS, Biden speaks on Israel-Hamas after meeting Xi): outcomes most likely come from the post-meeting readout/press conference held around or after 2023-11-16 00:00 UTC; only opening-of-meeting headlines (n0134, n0137, n0135) were used.
n1311 (moneywise.com, 'Best Online Mortgage Lenders of February 2024', stamped 2023-11-15 22:04): names a later month; misdated evergreen page, not used.

Date-only timestamps: n1555/n1556 (Japan Q3 GDP), n0222/n0223 (China October activity) and n0219 (PBOC MLF) are stamped 2023-11-14 08:00 although the releases occurred late on 2023-11-14 / early 2023-11-15 UTC; all releases precede the cutoff, so they were used as completed events.

Palo Alto Networks results (n0982, n0983, n0981): released after the 2023-11-15 U.S. close; the card's -1.91% PANW move is the regular session before the reaction, so no post-release price level is quoted.
Tencent results (n1021, n1304): the card's +4.81% 0700.HK session is not attributed to the results; no claim is made about the Hong Kong reaction.
Polish October CPI final revision (n1813, n1815, n1817): headlines give direction (slightly higher than the flash) but no figure, so no number is quoted.
No RPP November decision headline is in the own-date set; the policy stance is described only through Kotecki's call to hold rates longer (n1679) and the NBP projection (n1680).
Walmart and Lowe's results are pending (previews n1257, n1545 carry no date), so no date or outcome is stated.
